transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-19
Start: 11:00 AM PT (recorded)
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Dana Ruiz (Vectora Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Vectora Infra Lead), Priya Menon (Vectora PM)

Summary:
Quick QBR-style check-in focused on uptime incidents last month, autoscale behavior during spikes, unit-cost concerns for inference, and next steps to pilot a Dedicated pool with conservative autoscale and KMS-integrated key wrapping. Vectora is nervous about tail latency spikes and token burn during retries; wants clear SLOs and runbook before moving to Dedicated.

Topics: uptime incident review, autoscale tuning, cost math, pilot scope, security/KMS and audit logs, rollout timeline

[00:00] Sophie: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to run through last month's incidents, go over the autoscale behavior you saw, and map out the pilot for Dedicated capacity to address latency variance. Marcus and I are on to answer infra and perf questions.
[00:12] Dana: Hey — thanks, yeah we've had a couple of production slowdowns on the /generate route; spikes at 2am UTC and again during marketing blasts. We're trying to understand whether it's scheduling or warmup or just KV cache cold starts.
[00:24] Marcus: Right, can you share a sample request pattern, like sequence lengths and whether you use long context? That helps us pick batching and kv cache warm policies.
[00:35] Liam: I'll share traces — but quick note, our current autoscale policy is pretty reactive: CPU+GPU util > 70% scale up, but scale down is aggressive. We saw a lot of scaling churn which correlated with queueing.
[01:05] Sophie: That's consistent with what we expect; aggressive scale down + cold pools means tail latency. For Vectora's profile (you mentioned 1–1.5k qps bursts) a small steady baseline plus burst capacity is usually better.
[02:14] Dana: Cost is the other worry. When we left the burst on during the marketing event we burned tokens and the bill jumped unexpectedly. We need guardrails and clearer cost predictions.
[02:33] Marcus: Two levers: batching + prefix KV caching. The runtime supports continuous batching and auto-prefix cache — but if your requests have differing prefixes it's less helpful. Also quantization and model variant routing (smaller model for non-critical requests) help.
[03:01] Priya: Can you explain model routing again? We have some low-priority endpoints and would prefer cheaper fallbacks automatically.
[03:12] Marcus: Sure. You can set routing policies by route: e.g., high-priority -> phoenix-13b-8q (low latency), low-priority -> phoenix-7b-8q (cheaper). Redwood will fallback if the primary is at capacity. Note: transcript sometimes says 'phoenix' — internal model names got mangled in earlier notes — the catalog shows verified performance.
[04:00] Liam: Any SLO guarantees around failover? We can't have token duplication or double-charging in retries.
[04:15] Sophie: We offer SLA-backed latency targets on Dedicated tiers; for Hosted we provide best-effort latency promises and extensive tracing. For Dedicated we'll propose 99th perc latency SLO and agreed rollback windows. We'll also include audit logs for request/response ids so you can reconcile token counts.
[05:02] Dana: We also need KMS integration. All patient PII must be encrypted with customer-managed keys.
[05:18] Marcus: Private/KMS is supported on our Private offering; Dedicated can integrate with your KMS for key wrapping. The transcript may occasionally show K V cache as 'kv cash' in the notes — sorry about the ASR.
[06:10] Sophie: Let's walk through the incident timeline quickly — Liam, can you describe the 2am UTC event?
[06:18] Liam: Sure. At 01:57 UTC we saw a sudden 3x increase in long-form summarization requests, average seq length jumped to ~3,200 tokens, queuing increased, autoscaler spun up 3 nodes then scaled back after 4 min, but the cold-starts plus kv cache misses caused 95th perc latency to spike to 1.6s from baseline 0.45s.
[07:05] Marcus: That sequence length is important — our kernel selection for long contexts is different; we recommend pre-warming or reserving a dedicated shard for long-seq workloads, or quantized CPU fallback for non-critical async jobs.
[08:30] Sophie: For the pilot we suggest: 1) Dedicated pool with baseline capacity equal to median qps, 2) Autoscale policy with longer cool down, 3) Two routing tiers for model variants, 4) Cost cap alerts and a nightly cost runbook, 5) KMS integration in Private if Vectora requires CMEK.
[09:02] Priya: That sounds promising. What's the expected delta in monthly run-rate if we keep median baseline at 40% of observed peak vs current reactive policy?
[09:24] Sophie: Rough back-of-envelope: smoothing to baseline reduces burst spin-up (and wasted token retries) and reduces request retries that double-charge, so you may see 10-25% cost reduction in token spend depending on mix. We'll run actual math with your telemetry.
[10:15] Dana: Can Redwood provide the cost model template you used in the last trial? We tried to plug in our numbers but the tokenization differences and prompt templating confused the totals.
[10:30] Marcus: We'll send the spreadsheet. Note we sometimes mislabel units in automated notes — tokens vs effective tokens — we'll annotate the sheet.
[12:00] Liam: On SLA/incident handling: if we move to Dedicated what is the escalation path and MTTR commitments?
[12:20] Sophie: Dedicated plans include a defined on-call escalation, 4-hour initial response for Sev1 and an SLA earn-back/credit structure for availability drops. We'll include contact names in the engagement doc.
[13:05] Dana: One more security ask: audit logs must include request_id, model_version, and user_flags.
[13:18] Marcus: We can provide structured audit logs and deliver them via your S3/secure endpoint; retention window customizable. We'll also surface per-route token breakdowns in the Console.
[15:30] Priya: Can we do a short on-prem feasibility check? There are regulatory pockets where we may need an air-gapped deploy for a subset of workloads.
[15:45] Sophie: Yes, Private/on-prem is an option but it's a separate engagement; typical path is start with Dedicated to stabilize, then evaluate Private for regulated workloads. Timeline usually 6–12 weeks for on-prem packaging.
[18:00] Marcus: For the pilot we'll want a 2-week soak with synthetic traffic that mirrors your peak pattern (we'll provide the harness). We'll collect 95/99 latency, token burn, and cost-per-1000 tokens.
[20:05] Dana: That works. We need a clear success criteria: 95th perc latency under 1s for high-pri routes during 75% of synthetic peak, and no >20% month-over-month token growth outside product-driven traffic.
[21:00] Sophie: We'll take that as the success criteria. We'll also add rollback criteria.
[22:30] (short cross-talk, background noise)
[25:00] Sophie: Recap of next steps — I'll send pricing + pilot scope, Marcus will schedule the benchmark and share scripts, Liam will send traces and autoscale configs, Priya will confirm success criteria and internal stakeholders.
[26:12] Liam: One point — can you include a sample runbook for when autoscale thrashes? We want concrete steps: pin baseline, extend cooldown, drain nodes gracefully.
[26:35] Marcus: Yep, we'll attach a runbook template with play-by-play commands. Some lines in the transcript might show wrong product names — e.g., 'Redwood Dedecated' — please ignore those ASR artifacts.
[30:00] Dana: Fingers crossed. If the pilot reduces cost unpredictability, we can move to a reserved commit for Dedicated.
[30:15] Sophie: Great. We'll aim to have the pricing + spreadsheet to you by Friday. Marcus will run the bench once we have your sample traces (Liam).
[31:05] (participants briefly discuss calendar availability for kickoff)
[35:00] Sophie: Any closing security questions?
[35:12] Priya: Just to confirm: SOC2 docs, data flow diagrams, and support SLA templates — can you attach those in the follow-up email?
[35:25] Sophie: Yes, I'll attach SOC2 cert, the diagram, and an engagement SLA.
[36:10] Marcus: Also a note: in our internal notes some acronyms got jumbled — KMS showed as 'KSMS' — don't rely on the raw transcript for compliance.
[40:00] (background typing / silence)
[50:00] Quick micro-discussion about billing cycles and forecast alerts — Sophie explains usage-based vs committed pricing tiers and burst allowances.
[58:00] Final wrap: confirm action items and dates.
[60:00] Meeting ends; recording stopped.

Attachments mentioned (links to be shared in follow-up): pricing spreadsheet, dedicated pilot scope doc, runbook template, SOC2 cert, data flow diagram, benchmark harness repo

End of transcript.
